title: MHRA reforms and the UKCA pathway: where SEWA sits on the regulatory trajectory
subtitle: The 22 July 2025 international-reliance package and the UKCA Class IIb route
excerpt: MHRA's reform package introduced international reliance provisions and a streamlined UKCA marking route for innovative medical devices, including AI-based SaMD. For SEWA, the trajectory is clear.
content:
The UK regulatory trajectory

MHRA's 22 July 2025 reform package introduced international reliance provisions and a streamlined UKCA marking route for innovative medical devices, including AI-based software as a medical device. For SEWA, the trajectory is clear and the timeline is defined.

SEWA classifies as Class IIb under UK MDR 2002 (as amended) and EU MDR 2017/745 Rule 11. The regulatory pathway runs through three phases: a prospective shadow trial (6 months, primary endpoint door-to-alert under 5 minutes), an NIHR EME application, and ultimately a UKCA Class IIb submission (planned Q2 2027). Each phase is designed to build the independent clinical validation that the market demands.
author: Dolapo Ariyo
